name: Nullcell-F3
description: Nullcell-F3 is a closed-cell CNT aerogel foam developed by Tessera Materials, produced by freeze-casting a CNT suspension into a hierarchical porous structure and then critically point-drying to preserve the three-dimensional scaffold. The resulting material is 99.2% void by volume — lighter than almost any competing solid — while the CNT cell walls provide exceptional structural integrity under compression and outstanding thermal insulation across a range from cryogenic to 1,400°C. Its acoustic damping properties are a secondary benefit that has driven significant adoption in architectural and vehicle applications.
applications: acoustic isolation panels in data centers
story_hooks: Nullcell-F3 panels in a Shelf district hab-block were substituted with standard foam during construction — when a fire breaks out, the building's thermal ratings are fiction.

Someone is using Nullcell-F3's acoustic damping properties to create a soundproofed room inside an existing structure that doesn't appear on any scan — a hidden space inside a building that should be solid.

A researcher discovers that Nullcell-F3 can be functionalized post-production to absorb specific chemical agents — and that someone has been doing exactly this to panels installed in a government facility's HVAC system.
